is_anopheles.evidence: The study evaluates females of the African malaria vector species Anopheles gambiae and An. arabiensis (Page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study uses mid-infrared spectroscopy to predict mosquito species and age structure; it does not report genotyping for any target insecticide resistance markers.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotype or allele counts/frequencies for resistance markers are reported.

african_field_population.evidence: The study used laboratory colony mosquitoes (An. gambiae Kisumu strain and An. arabiensis Ifakara strain reared at the University of Glasgow) rather than field-caught African populations (Page 4).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study evaluating mid-infrared spectroscopy and machine learning algorithms (Page 1-5).

sub_country_location.evidence: Not applicable as only laboratory colonies were analyzed.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: No field collection date window is reported as only laboratory colonies were used.

duplicate_risk.evidence: Methodological laboratory colony study with no field data overlap.

supplement.evidence: No supplementary material is needed as the paper does not report target resistance marker data.

assessment.summary: This study demonstrates a machine-learning method using mid-infrared spectroscopy (MIRS) to predict the species identity and age structure of laboratory-reared Anopheles gambiae s.s. and Anopheles arabiensis. It does not report any target insecticide resistance marker genotyping data or field-collected mosquito populations.
exclusion_reasons: Does not report target insecticide-resistance markers
Does not report extractable genotype data
Does not evaluate African field populations (uses laboratory colonies only)
